stories.headline: AI chip startup Etched exits stealth with $800M raised and $1B in orders

key_facts.fact: Etched came out of stealth on July 1, 2026, disclosing $800 million raised to date and more than $1 billion in customer contracts already booked.
key_facts.excerpt: AI chip startup Etched has stepped out of stealth with a significant progress report: $800 million raised to date, $1 billion in contract orders already booked, and a first chip successfully manufactured by TSMC earlier this year.

key_facts.fact: Etched's first chip was manufactured by TSMC earlier in 2026 following a successful A0 tapeout, and the company is now testing its debut product, a 'frontier inference cluster,' with early customers.
key_facts.excerpt: Etched announced that it has come out of stealth after building its first racks following a successful A0 tapeout.

key_facts.fact: Its most recent funding was a $500 million round closed in December at a $5 billion post-money valuation, led by Stripes with participation from Jane Street, Hudson River Trading, Two Sigma, Ribbit Capital and VentureTech Alliance, which has a strategic partnership with TSMC.
key_facts.excerpt: It was earlier reported that Etched raised a $500 million round valuing the company at $5 billion. Led by investment firm Stripes with participation from billionaire Peter Thiel, Positive Sum and Ribbit Capital, that round closed in December and also included an investment from Jane Street, Hudson River Trading, Two Sigma and VentureTech Alliance.

key_facts.fact: Jane Street has invested a total of more than $100 million in Etched, and the company plans to start shipping chips to some customers this summer.
key_facts.excerpt: The trading firm has invested a total of more than $100 million in Etched, according to people familiar with the matter... The aspiring competitor to Nvidia plans to start shipping chips to some customers this summer.

key_facts.fact: Founded in 2022 by Harvard dropouts Gavin Uberti (CEO) and Robert Wachen (President), Etched designs chips to run AI inference; angel investors include Geoffrey Hinton, Andrej Karpathy, Fei-Fei Li, Arthur Mensch, Stanley Druckenmiller and Peter Thiel.
key_facts.excerpt: Angel investors include AI luminaries Andrej Karpathy, Geoffrey Hinton, Fei-Fei Li, Arthur Mensch, and Scott Wu, alongside billionaires Stanley Druckenmiller and Peter Thiel.

stories.headline: Data center operator Switch seeks $2B round led by a16z at nearly $50B valuation

key_facts.fact: Data center operator Switch has launched a private funding round led by Andreessen Horowitz that could raise about $2 billion and value the company at nearly $50 billion including debt, Bloomberg reported on Thursday, July 2.
key_facts.excerpt: Data center operator Switch has launched a private funding round led by venture capital firm Andreessen Horowitz that could raise about $2 billion and value the company at nearly $50 billion including debt, Bloomberg News reported on Thursday.

key_facts.fact: Andreessen Horowitz is expected to invest roughly $400 million, while Goldman Sachs and JPMorgan Chase are working on the financing.
key_facts.excerpt: Andreessen Horowitz is expected to invest roughly $400 million, while Goldman Sachs and JPMorgan Chase are working on the financing.

key_facts.fact: The round would value Switch's equity at about $19 billion before the new investment.
key_facts.excerpt: The company would have an equity value of about $19 billion not including the latest investment, the people said.

key_facts.fact: The financing would precede a potential IPO as soon as next year; Las Vegas-based Switch is majority-owned by DigitalBridge Group, which together with IFM Investors acquired it in a 2022 deal valued at $11 billion including debt.
key_facts.excerpt: Bloomberg said the financing would precede a potential initial public offering as soon as next year... Las Vegas-based Switch is majority-owned by Digitalbridge Group (NYSE:DBRG), which, together with IFM Investors, acquired the company in a 2022 deal valued at $11 billion including debt.

stories.headline: SK Hynix amends SEC filing for record Nasdaq listing, adds DRAM antitrust suit risk

key_facts.fact: SK Hynix amended its Form F-1/A with the SEC on Wednesday, July 1, 2026, adding a newly initiated antitrust class action to its 'Risk Factors' ahead of its planned Nasdaq ADR listing.
key_facts.excerpt: According to its amended Form F-1/A filed with the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) on Wednesday, the company added a newly initiated antitrust class action to its 'Risk Factors.'

key_facts.fact: The lawsuit, filed June 25 in the Northern District of California by 14 U.S. consumers and three PC manufacturers, alleges SK Hynix, Samsung and Micron conspired to restrict commodity DRAM supply and inflate prices from around October 2022.
key_facts.excerpt: The lawsuit, filed on June 25 in the U.S. District Court for the Northern District of California by indirect purchasers of commodity DRAM products, alleges that SK hynix, along with Samsung Electronics and Micron, conspired to restrict supply and inflate prices beginning around October 2022.

key_facts.fact: SK Hynix reiterated it will use listing proceeds to expand domestic production and buy EUV lithography equipment, planning to invest roughly 11.9 trillion won ($8.6 billion) in EUV deliveries by the end of 2027.
key_facts.excerpt: SK hynix reiterated its plan to use the proceeds to fund its domestic production facility expansion and the acquisition of extreme ultraviolet (EUV) lithography equipment. The company plans to invest approximately 11.9 trillion won ($8.6 billion) in EUV equipment deliveries expected by the end of 2027.

key_facts.fact: The company disclosed a 56.4% global market share in High Bandwidth Memory (HBM) and 29.1% share of the broader DRAM market based on Q1 IDC data.
key_facts.excerpt: The chipmaker also disclosed its market position based on first-quarter data from research firm IDC, citing a 56.4 percnet global market share in High Bandwidth Memory (HBM) and a 29.1 percent share in the broader DRAM market.

key_facts.fact: SK Hynix plans to raise up to $29.4 billion by issuing up to 17.79 million new shares in the ADR listing on Nasdaq under symbol 'SKHY', with trading expected to begin July 10; at the top of its range it would be the largest ADR offering on record.
key_facts.excerpt: SK hynix aims to raise up to 45.45 trillion won, about $29 billion, by issuing up to 17.79 million new shares... If the offering prices at the top of its range, it would be the largest ADR offering on record, surpassing the $21.8 billion Alibaba raised in its 2014 New York debut.

stories.headline: Samsung unveils 2nm and 1.4nm foundry roadmap at SAFE Forum 2026 to win AI chip clients

key_facts.fact: Samsung Electronics' foundry division unveiled its next-generation technology roadmap on Tuesday, July 1, at the SAFE (Samsung Advanced Foundry Ecosystem) Forum 2026 at its Seocho headquarters in Seoul, under the theme 'The Nexus for Silicon Intelligence.'
key_facts.excerpt: Samsung Electronics' foundry division unveiled its next-generation technology roadmap Tuesday at the SAFE (Samsung Advanced Foundry Ecosystem) Forum 2026, laying out its strategy to win over global AI semiconductor customers.

key_facts.fact: Samsung announced the mass production roadmap for third-generation 2nm and second-generation 1.4nm chips at the forum.
key_facts.excerpt: During the SAFE Forum 2026 event, Samsung Foundry announced the mass production roadmap for third-gen 2nm and second-gen 1.4nm chips.

key_facts.fact: Samsung reaffirmed plans to begin mass production of its 1.4nm process in 2029 and set an enhanced SF1.4+ node for 2030, per VP Shin Jong-shin.
key_facts.excerpt: Samsung Electronics Co. (Samsung) reaffirmed its plan to begin mass production of its 1.4-nanometer (nm) process in 2029, confirming the revised roadmap it announced last year.

key_facts.fact: Samsung highlighted SRAM technology, which drew attention after being adopted in Nvidia's first AI inference-dedicated chip, the Groq3 language processing unit; the forum drew about 400 attendees from client and partner companies.
key_facts.excerpt: The company highlighted plans to strengthen its SRAM (static random-access memory) technology — which drew attention after being adopted in Nvidia's first AI inference-dedicated chip, the Groq3 language processing unit... The annual event... drew about 400 attendees from client and partner companies.

stories.headline: Raja Koduri's Oxmiq Labs raises $35M to cut the cost of designing custom AI chips

key_facts.fact: AI chipmaking startup Oxmiq Labs said on July 1, 2026 that it raised $35 million in an early-stage Series A, bringing its total raised to date to $60 million.
key_facts.excerpt: Artificial intelligence chipmaking startup Oxmiq Labs Inc. says it wants to become the next Arm Holdings Plc. after raising $35 million in an early-stage A funding, bringing its total amount raised to date to $60 million.

key_facts.fact: The round was led by Fundomo and the Samsung Catalyst Fund, with participation from MediaTek, AM Intelligence Labs, Pegatron Venture Capital, CDIB-TEN, Darwin Ventures and Morgan Creek Digital.
key_facts.excerpt: Today's Series A round was led by investors that included Fundomo and Samsung Catalyst Fund, and saw participation from MediaTek, AM Intelligence Labs, Pegatron Venture Capital, CDIB-TEN, Darwin Ventures and Morgan Creek Digital.

key_facts.fact: Oxmiq is founded and led by GPU architect Raja Koduri, former chief architect and EVP of Intel's architecture, graphics and software division; the funds will scale its proprietary GPU architecture OxCore, which lets firms design custom silicon without a full chip program.
key_facts.excerpt: Oxmiq is founded and led by the respected graphics processing unit architect Raja Koduri, who formerly served as the chief architect and Executive Vice President of Intel Corp.'s architecture, graphics and software division... The funds from today's round will help to scale Oxmiq's proprietary GPU architecture OxCore, which makes it easier for semiconductor firms and AI systems builders to design custom silicon without a full chip program.

stories.headline: Apptronik opens expanded Robot Park and introduces Apollo 2 humanoid platform

key_facts.fact: On July 1, 2026 Apptronik expanded its Robot Park facility in Austin, Texas, to nearly 90,000 square feet as a flagship training and data-collection site for humanoid robots designed for industrial and commercial work.
key_facts.excerpt: Apptronik expanded its nearly 90,000-square-foot Robot Park facility in Austin, Texas, and introduced Apollo 2 as it gathers more real-world data for humanoid robots designed for industrial and commercial work.

key_facts.fact: The company introduced Apollo 2, available in bipedal and wheeled-base configurations, already operating across Robot Park and at customer and partner sites including Google DeepMind, Mercedes-Benz and GXO.
key_facts.excerpt: Apollo 2 is available in bipedal and wheeled-base configurations and is already operating across Robot Park and at customer and partner sites, including Google DeepMind, Mercedes-Benz and GXO.

key_facts.fact: Data collected by Apollo 2 supports Apptronik's research partnership with Google DeepMind and helps advance Gemini Robotics, DeepMind's foundation AI models for robotics; the data also feeds development of the next-generation Apollo 3.
key_facts.excerpt: The initiative supports Apptronik's research partnership with Google DeepMind, where data gathered by Apollo 2 contributes to advancing Gemini Robotics AI models for future humanoid robot deployment across industries.

key_facts.fact: Apptronik announced in February it had closed a $520 million Series A-X extension, bringing total Series A financing to more than $935 million and total capital raised to nearly $1 billion.
key_facts.excerpt: Apptronik announced in February it had closed a $520 million Series A-X extension, bringing its total Series A financing to more than $935 million and total capital raised to nearly $1 billion.

stories.headline: National Grid Ventures to invest $1.75B in Joulent for U.S. data center power

key_facts.fact: National Grid Ventures agreed on July 1, 2026 to invest $1.75 billion for a 35% stake in Joulent LLC, forming a strategic partnership to develop contracted power and electrical infrastructure for U.S. large-load demand including data centers.
key_facts.excerpt: National Grid Ventures (NGV), the commercial arm of National Grid plc, has agreed to invest $1.75 billion for a 35% stake in Joulent LLC, forming a broad strategic partnership to develop contracted power and electrical infrastructure solutions for U.S. large load demand.

key_facts.fact: The investment will enable Joulent's foundational Project Kilby, a 2.67 GW co-located power facility in West Texas built in a 50/50 partnership with Chevron, supplying dedicated electricity to a Microsoft-operated data center under a 20-year power purchase agreement.
key_facts.excerpt: NGV's investment will enable the development of Joulent's foundational project, Project Kilby ('Kilby'), in a 50/50 partnership with Chevron Corporation. Kilby is a 2.67 GW co-located power facility in West Texas that will provide dedicated electricity to a Microsoft-operated data center under a 20-year power purchase agreement.

key_facts.fact: Project Kilby has secured critical equipment including GE Vernova turbines and reserved EPC capacity, targeting first power delivery by 2028, with a final investment decision expected in 2026.
key_facts.excerpt: Development of the project is at an advanced stage with secured critical equipment including GE Vernova turbines and reserved EPC capacity, and it is targeting first power delivery by 2028... with a final investment decision expected in 2026.

key_facts.fact: The investment is incremental to National Grid's existing five-year capital program of at least £70 billion (about $90 billion) through 2031; the company expects to connect more than 10 GW of data center demand across the U.K. and U.S. over the next five years.
key_facts.excerpt: The investment is incremental to National Grid's existing five-year capital investment program of at least £70 billion (approximately $90 billion) through 2031... where it expects to connect more than 10 GW of demand across the U.K. and U.S. over the next five years.
